patterns.label: Want to do something
patterns.note: 我想 (ngo5 soeng2) means 'I want to' — attach any verb to say what you'd like to do. The most useful starter for expressing intention.

examples.e: I want to watch a movie

drills.frameJ: ngo5 soeng2 ▢.
drills.english: I want to watch a movie.

patterns.label: Want or need something
patterns.note: 我要 (ngo5 jiu3) means 'I want / I need' followed by a thing — ordering, shopping, asking for what you need. Stronger and more direct than 我想 (ngo5 soeng2).

drills.frameJ: ngo5 jiu3 ▢
drills.english: I'll have water

drills.frameJ: tau4 tung3, heoi3 joek6 fong2 maai5 di1 ▢.
drills.english: Headache — go to the pharmacy for some medicine.
drills.frameE: Headache — go to the pharmacy for some …

drills.frameJ: jap6 heoi3 zi1 cin4 jiu3 maai5 ▢.
drills.english: Before going in you need to buy a ticket.
drills.frameE: Before going in you need to buy a …

patterns.label: Do you have…?
patterns.note: 有冇 (jau5 mou5) literally 'have-not-have' — the everyday way to ask whether something is available. Put the thing you're after right after it.

drills.frameJ: jau5 mou5 ▢?
drills.english: Do you have dim sum?

drills.frameJ: lou5 baan2, ▢ ngo5 jiu3 maai5 saam1 gin6.
drills.english: Boss, any discount? I want three.

drills.frameJ: ni1 gin6 taai3 sai3, jau5 mou5 ▢?
drills.english: This one's too small — got a large?
drills.frameE: This one's too small — got a …?

patterns.label: There's also…
patterns.note: 重有 (zung6 jau5) means 'there's also / and also' — adding one more item to a list or order.

drills.frameJ: zung6 jau5 ▢.
drills.english: There's also noodles.

patterns.label: Please give me…
patterns.note: 唔該畀 (m4 goi1 bei2) — 'please give me' — a polite request to be handed something. 唔該 (m4 goi1) is the everyday 'please'.

drills.frameJ: si6 jing3, m4 goi1 bei2 go3 ▢ ngo5 dei6.
drills.english: Waiter, please give us a menu.

patterns.label: Can I / May I?
patterns.structure: 可以 (ho2 ji5) + [verb] + 得唔得 (dak1 m4 dak1)?
patterns.note: 可以…得唔得 (ho2 ji5…dak1 m4 dak1) asks permission — 'can I…?'. Wrap the verb you want to do between them.

examples.j: ho2 ji5 co5 dak1 m4 dak1?
ho2 ji5 jap6 dak1 m4 dak1?
ho2 ji5 si3 dak1 m4 dak1?

patterns.label: Have to / need to
patterns.note: 要 (jiu3) before a verb means 'have to / need to' — an obligation rather than a wish. (Before a noun, 要 means 'want', as in 我要水 ngo5 jiu3 seoi2.)

patterns.label: I like…
patterns.note: 鍾意 (zung1 ji3) is the everyday 'like'. Place anything you favour after it — a thing, an activity, a person. No tense marker needed for stable preferences.

drills.frameJ: ngo5 zung1 ji3 ▢.
drills.english: I like dogs.

drills.frameJ: ngo5 zung1 ji3 ▢, hou2 ci5 pou4 tou4.
drills.english: I like purple, like grapes.

drills.frameC: 我嘅興趣係▢,週末成日去。
drills.frameJ: ngo5 ge3 hing3 ceoi3 hai6 ▢, zau1 mut6 sing4 jat6 heoi3.
drills.english: My hobby is hiking — I go every weekend.
drills.frameE: My hobby is … — I go every weekend.

drills.frameJ: ngo5 heoi3 KTV ▢.
drills.english: I go to KTV to sing.

drills.frameJ: fung1 ging2 hou2 leng3, ngo5 soeng2 ▢.
drills.english: The scenery is beautiful — I want to take photos.
drills.frameE: The scenery is beautiful — I want to …

drills.frameJ: jam1 ngok6 jat1 hoeng2, keoi5 zau6 hoi1 ci2 ▢.
drills.english: As soon as the music plays, she starts to dance.
drills.frameE: As soon as the music plays, she starts to …

patterns.label: I feel…
patterns.note: 覺得 (gok3 dak1) means 'feel / think' — use it to report an emotion or opinion, usually with 好 (hou2, very) plus an adjective.

examples.j: ngo5 gok3 dak1 hou2 hoi1 sam1

drills.frameJ: ngo5 gok3 dak1 hou2 ▢.
drills.english: I feel really happy.

patterns.label: Very / too + adjective
patterns.note: 好 (hou2, very) and 太 (taai3, too) go directly before an adjective to describe something — 好熱 (hou2 jit6, very hot), 太貴 (taai3 gwai3, too expensive). 太 (taai3) carries a sense of 'excessively'.

drills.frameJ: ngo5 hou2 ▢.
drills.english: I'm very tired.

drills.frameJ: gam1 jat6 hou2 ▢.
drills.english: It's very hot today.

drills.frameJ: taai3 ▢ laa3!
drills.english: Too expensive!

drills.frameJ: keoi5 sing4 jat6 bong1 jan4, hou2 ▢.
drills.english: She always helps people, she's very kind.
drills.frameE: She always helps people, she's very …

drills.frameJ: ting1 jat6 haau2 si5, ngo5 hou2 ▢.
drills.english: Exam tomorrow — I'm very nervous.

drills.frameJ: keoi5 jat6 jat6 nou5 lik6 zou6 je5, hou2 ▢.
drills.english: He works hard every day — very hardworking.
drills.frameE: He works hard every day — very …

drills.frameJ: dung1 tin1 lai4 laa3, gam1 jat6 hou2 ▢.
drills.english: Winter's here — it's cold today.

drills.frameJ: faan1 ciu4 laa3, gaan1 uk1 hou2 ▢.
drills.english: It's the wet season — the flat is very humid.
drills.frameE: It's the wet season — the flat is very …

drills.frameJ: haang4 lou6 zau6 dou3, hou2 ▢.
drills.english: You can walk there — it's very close.
drills.frameE: You can walk there — it's very …

drills.frameJ: ni1 tiu4 fu3 taai3 ▢, zoek3 m4 lok6.
drills.english: These trousers are too tight — can't get them on.
drills.frameE: These trousers are too … — can't get them on.

drills.frameC: 啲點心真係好▢,我要再叫。
drills.frameJ: di1 dim2 sam1 zan1 hai6 hou2 ▢, ngo5 jiu3 zoi3 giu3.
drills.english: The dim sum is really delicious — I'll order more.
drills.frameE: The dim sum is really … — I'll order more.

drills.frameJ: ngo5 sing4 jat6 mei6 sik6 faan6, hou2 ▢.
drills.english: I haven't eaten all day, I'm very hungry.
drills.frameE: I haven't eaten all day, I'm very …

drills.frameJ: zek3 tou3 zai2 mou4 jung4 jung4, zan1 hai6 hou2 ▢.
drills.english: The rabbit is fluffy — really so cute.
drills.frameE: The rabbit is fluffy — really so …

patterns.label: A bit more / less
patterns.note: 啲 (di1) after an adjective softens it to 'a bit / -er' — 平啲 (peng4 di1, a bit cheaper), 快啲 (faai3 di1, a bit faster). Handy for polite requests and comparisons.

patterns.label: This is…
patterns.note: 呢個係 (ni1 go3 hai6) — 'this is' — introduces or identifies something or someone. 係 (hai6) is the verb 'to be'. Swap 呢個 (ni1 go3, this) for 嗰個 (go2 go3, that) at a distance.

examples.j: ni1 go3 hai6 ngo5 baa4 baa1

drills.frameJ: ni1 go3 hai6 ngo5 ▢.
drills.english: This is my father.

drills.frameJ: ngo5 ▢ hou2 sek3 ngo5.
drills.english: My mother loves me very much.

drills.frameC: 佢教我哋讀書,係我哋嘅▢。
drills.frameJ: keoi5 gaau3 ngo5 dei6 duk6 syu1, hai6 ngo5 dei6 ge3 ▢.
drills.english: She teaches us — she's our teacher.

drills.frameJ: keoi5 tung4 ngo5 jat1 cai4 zou6 je5, hai6 ngo5 ▢.
drills.english: He works with me — he's my colleague.
drills.frameE: He works with me — he's my …

drills.frameJ: ngo5 jung6 ▢ daa2 zi6 tung4 soeng5 mong5.
drills.english: I use a computer to type and go online.
drills.frameE: I use a … to type and go online.

drills.frameJ: ngo5 jung6 ▢ lo2 je5.
drills.english: I use my hand to pick things up.
drills.frameE: I use my … to pick things up.

drills.frameJ: m4 sik1 lou6, ho2 ji5 tai2 haa5 ▢.
drills.english: Don't know the way — can look at the map.
drills.frameE: Don't know the way — can look at the …

patterns.label: I have…
patterns.note: 我有 (ngo5 jau5) means 'I have'. Also used for conditions and symptoms — 我有頭痛 (ngo5 jau5 tau4 tung3, I have a headache). The negative is 我冇 (ngo5 mou5, I don't have).

drills.frameJ: ngo5 jau5 loeng5 go3 ▢.
drills.english: I have two daughters.

drills.frameJ: ngo5 ▢, soeng2 fan3 gaau3.
drills.english: I have a headache, I want to sleep.
drills.frameE: I have a …, I want to sleep.

drills.frameJ: ngo5 hou2 jit6, ho2 nang4 ▢.
drills.english: I feel hot — maybe I have a fever.
drills.frameE: I feel hot — maybe I have a …

drills.frameC: 我屋企養咗一隻▢,成日捉老鼠。
drills.frameJ: ngo5 uk1 kei2 joeng5 zo2 jat1 zek3 ▢, sing4 jat6 zuk1 lou5 syu2.
drills.english: I keep a cat at home — it always catches mice.
drills.frameE: I keep a … at home — it always catches mice.

drills.frameC: 農場有一隻▢,可以畀人騎。
drills.frameJ: nung4 coeng4 jau5 jat1 zek3 ▢, ho2 ji5 bei2 jan4 ke4.
drills.english: The farm has a horse you can ride.
drills.frameE: The farm has a … you can ride.

patterns.label: Not / don't
patterns.note: Two negatives: 唔 (m4) negates a verb or adjective — 唔要 (m4 jiu3, don't want), 唔貴 (m4 gwai3, not expensive); 冇 (mou5) means 'have not / there isn't' — 冇水 (mou5 seoi2, no water).

patterns.label: X is at / located
patterns.note: 喺 (hai2) means 'at / in / on' — it links a thing to where it is. 喺邊度 (hai2 bin1 dou6) asks 'where is it?'.

drills.frameJ: ▢ hai2 bin1 dou6?
drills.english: Where is the MTR?

drills.frameJ: ngan4 hong4 hai2 ▢, m4 hai6 jau6 bin1.
drills.english: The bank is on the left, not the right.
drills.frameE: The bank is on the …, not the right.

drills.frameJ: ce1 zaam6 hai2 ▢, haang4 do1 gei2 bou6 zau6 dou3.
drills.english: The station is ahead — a few more steps and you're there.
drills.frameE: The station is … — a few more steps and you're there.

drills.frameC: 超市就喺▢,過條馬路就到。
drills.frameJ: ciu1 si5 zau6 hai2 ▢, gwo3 tiu4 maa5 lou6 zau6 dou3.
drills.english: The supermarket is right opposite — cross the road and you're there.
drills.frameE: The supermarket is right … — cross the road and you're there.

drills.frameJ: gau3 jan4 laa3, heoi3 ▢ tek3 bo1 laa1.
drills.english: We have enough people — let's go to the field to play.
drills.frameE: We have enough people — let's go to the … to play.

drills.frameJ: ngo5 jiu3 lo2 jin6 gam1, heoi3 ▢.
drills.english: I need cash — go to the bank.
drills.frameE: I need cash — go to the …

drills.frameJ: tou5 o1, soeng2 heoi3 ▢.
drills.english: Upset stomach — need the toilet.

drills.frameJ: je6 laa3, ngo5 jiu3 faan1 ▢ fan3 gaau3.
drills.english: It's late — I need to go home to sleep.
drills.frameE: It's late — I need to go … to sleep.

patterns.label: Go to a place
patterns.note: 去 (heoi3) means 'go to'. Follow it with a destination — 去酒店 (heoi3 zau2 dim3, go to the hotel). Add a verb after the place for purpose — 去公司返工 (heoi3 gung1 si1 faan1 gung1).

drills.frameJ: ngo5 heoi3 ▢.
drills.english: I'm going to the hotel.

drills.frameJ: beng6 dak1 hou2 jim4 zung6, jiu3 heoi3 ▢.
drills.english: Seriously ill — need to go to the hospital.
drills.frameE: Seriously ill — need to go to the …

drills.frameJ: m4 sai2 zyun3, jat1 zik6 ▢ zau6 dak1.
drills.english: No need to turn — just go straight.
drills.frameE: No need to turn — just … and you're fine.

patterns.label: Time word first
patterns.note: Cantonese puts the time at the START of the sentence, before the action — 今日 (gam1 jat6, today), 聽日 (ting1 jat6, tomorrow), 琴日 (kam4 jat6, yesterday), 朝早 (ziu1 zou2, morning).

drills.frameJ: ▢ gin3!
drills.english: See you tomorrow!

drills.frameJ: ▢ sik6 zou2 caan1.
drills.english: Eat breakfast in the morning.

drills.frameJ: ▢ lok6 jyu5.
drills.english: It rained yesterday.

patterns.label: See you at / on…
patterns.note: 見 (gin3) means 'see / meet'. Tack it after a time to make a casual farewell — 聽日見 (ting1 jat6 gin3, see you tomorrow), 星期一見 (sing1 kei4 jat1 gin3, see you Monday).

patterns.label: Who? (邊個 bin1 go3)
patterns.note: 邊個 (bin1 go3) means 'who / which one'. Place it where the unknown person goes in the sentence.

drills.frameJ: ▢ hai6 nei5 ge3 lou5 si1?
drills.english: Who is your teacher?

patterns.label: What? (乜嘢 mat1 je5)
patterns.note: 乜嘢 (mat1 je5) means 'what'. In Cantonese it usually comes at the END of the question, not the start — 你食乜嘢 (nei5 sik6 mat1 je5)? = 'you eat what?'.

drills.frameJ: ni1 go3 hai6 ▢?
drills.english: What is this?

patterns.label: Where? (邊度 bin1 dou6)
patterns.note: 邊度 (bin1 dou6) means 'where'. Like 乜嘢 (mat1 je5), it usually sits at the end of the question.

drills.frameJ: nei5 zyu6 hai2 ▢?
drills.english: Where do you live?

drills.frameJ: si1 gei1 man6: ▢
drills.english: The driver asks: Where to?

patterns.label: When? (幾時 gei2 si4)
patterns.note: 幾時 (gei2 si4) means 'when'. Often appears near the start — 幾時去？ (gei2 si4 heoi3?, when are we going?).

drills.frameJ: ▢ heoi3 sik6 faan6?
drills.english: When are we going to eat?

patterns.label: Why? (點解 dim2 gaai2)
patterns.note: 點解 (dim2 gaai2) means 'why' — literally 'how to explain'. Use it to ask the reason for something.

drills.frameJ: nei5 ▢ m4 lai4?
drills.english: Why aren't you coming?

patterns.label: How much / many?
patterns.structure: 幾錢 (gei2 cin2) / 幾多 (gei2 do1)
patterns.note: 幾多 (gei2 do1) asks 'how many / how much' of something; 幾錢 (gei2 cin2) specifically asks a price — 'how much money'.

drills.frameJ: nei5 jau5 ▢ bun2 syu1?
drills.english: How many books do you have?

drills.frameJ: A: ▢ B: ng5 sap6 man1.
drills.english: How much? — Fifty dollars.

patterns.label: How far / how long?
patterns.structure: 幾遠 (gei2 jyun5) / 幾耐 (gei2 noi6)
patterns.note: 幾遠 (gei2 jyun5) asks distance — 'how far'; 幾耐 (gei2 noi6) asks duration — 'how long'. Both pair a destination or activity with 幾 (gei2, how).

drills.frameJ: si1 gei1, heoi3 gei1 coeng4 ▢
drills.english: Driver, how far is it to the airport?

drills.frameJ: soeng2 heoi3 bok3 mat6 gun2, sin1 man6 ▢
drills.english: Want to go to the museum — first ask what time it opens.
drills.frameE: Want to go to the museum — first ask …

patterns.label: Completed action (咗 zo2)
patterns.note: 咗 (zo2) after a verb marks it as done — like English '-ed'. 食咗 (sik6 zo2, ate), 去咗 (heoi3 zo2, went). The single most useful tense marker.

drills.frameJ: ngo5 sik6 ▢ faan6.
drills.english: I have eaten.

patterns.label: In progress (緊 gan2)
patterns.note: 緊 (gan2) after a verb means the action is happening right now — like English '-ing'. 食緊 (sik6 gan2, eating), 做緊 (zou6 gan2, doing).

drills.frameJ: ngo5 sik6 ▢ faan6, dang2 zan6 sin1.
drills.english: I'm eating right now, wait a bit.

patterns.label: Experienced before (過 gwo3)
patterns.note: 過 (gwo3) after a verb marks past experience — 'have you ever…'. 食過 (sik6 gwo3, have eaten before), 去過 (heoi3 gwo3, have been to).

drills.frameJ: ngo5 heoi3 ▢ hoeng1 gong2.
drills.english: I've been to Hong Kong before.

patterns.label: Will / going to (會 wui5)
patterns.note: 會 (wui5) before a verb marks the future — 'will'. 我會去 (ngo5 wui5 heoi3, I will go). For obligation use 要 (jiu3, need to) instead.

drills.frameJ: ting1 jat6 ▢ lok6 jyu5.
drills.english: It will rain tomorrow.

patterns.label: Already / not yet (已經 ji5 ging1 / 未 mei6)
patterns.note: 已經 (ji5 ging1, already) and 未 (mei6, not yet) are a natural pair for 'done or not?'. 已經食咗 (ji5 ging1 sik6 zo2, already eaten); 未食 (mei6 sik6, haven't eaten yet).

drills.frameJ: ngo5 ▢ sik6 zo2 laa3.
drills.english: I've already eaten.

patterns.label: Yes/no question (嗎 maa3)
patterns.note: 嗎 (maa3) at the end of a statement turns it into a yes/no question — the simplest way to ask.

drills.frameJ: nei5 sik6 zo2 faan6 ▢?
drills.english: Have you eaten?

patterns.label: Suggestion (啦 laa1)
patterns.note: 啦 (laa1) softens a suggestion or request into something friendly — 'come on, let's…'. 走啦 (zau2 laa1, let's go).

drills.frameJ: ngo5 dei6 zau2 ▢!
drills.english: Let's get going!

patterns.label: Change of state (喇 laa3)
patterns.note: 喇 (laa3) signals something has changed or is now the case — 'now'. 好喇 (hou2 laa3, OK now / that's enough).

drills.frameJ: ngo5 sik6 baau2 ▢.
drills.english: I'm full now.

patterns.label: Surprise (咩 me1)
patterns.note: 咩 (me1) at the end expresses surprise or doubt — 'really? / is that so?'. 真係咩 (zan1 hai6 me1, is that really true?).

drills.frameJ: keoi5 zau2 zo2 ▢? zan1 hai6 gu2 m4 dou2.
drills.english: He's left, really? I'm surprised.

patterns.label: Matter-of-fact (㗎 gaa3)
patterns.note: 㗎 (gaa3) states something as plain fact — 'that's just how it is'. 係㗎 (hai6 gaa3, yes, that's right).

drills.frameJ: keoi5 hai6 lou5 si1 ▢, m4 hou2 waai4 ji4.
drills.english: He's a teacher, that's a fact — don't doubt it.
drills.frameE: He's a teacher … — don't doubt it.

patterns.label: Counting up
patterns.note: Cantonese counts like reciting numbers in English: 一二三四五 (jat1 ji6 saam1 sei3 ng5). The first ten are the foundation for every larger number.

drills.frameJ: jat1, ji6, ▢, sei3, ng5.
drills.english: One, two, three, four, five.

patterns.label: Tens & hundreds
patterns.note: Build bigger numbers by putting a digit in front: 二十 (ji6 sap6, twenty), 三十 (saam1 sap6, thirty), 一百 (jat1 baak3, a hundred), 五百 (ng5 baak3, five hundred).

drills.frameJ: ni1 go3 ▢ man1.
drills.english: This is one hundred dollars.

drills.frameJ: ngo5 jau5 ▢ man1.
drills.english: I have fifty dollars.

patterns.label: Half (一半 jat1 bun3)
patterns.note: 一半 (jat1 bun3) means 'half'. Use it before a measure word + noun — 一半個西瓜 (jat1 bun3 go3 sai1 gwaa1, half a watermelon).

drills.frameJ: ngo5 sik6 zo2 ▢ go3 sai1 gwaa1.
drills.english: I ate half of the watermelon.

patterns.label: How long does it take?
patterns.note: 幾耐 (gei2 noi6) asks about duration — 'how long'. 要幾耐 (jiu3 gei2 noi6, how long does it take). 耐 (noi6) means a length of time.

patterns.label: Together / let's
patterns.note: 一齊 (jat1 cai4) means 'together'. Put it before a verb to suggest doing something jointly — 一齊去 (jat1 cai4 heoi3, let's go together).

drills.frameC: 唔好留喺屋企,我哋▢出街啦。
drills.frameJ: m4 hou2 lau4 hai2 uk1 kei2, ngo5 dei6 ▢ ceot1 gaai1 laa1.
drills.english: Don't stay home — let's go out together.
drills.frameE: Don't stay home — let's go out … .

patterns.label: First… then…
patterns.note: 先…再… (sin1…zoi3…) sequences two actions — 'first… then…'. 先食飯再走 (sin1 sik6 faan6 zoi3 zau2, eat first, then go).

examples.j: sin1 paai4 deoi2 zoi3 jap6 coeng4

patterns.label: Give someone something
patterns.note: 畀 (bei2) means 'give'. The order is 畀 + thing + person — 畀錢佢 (bei2 cin2 keoi5, give him the money). Also means 'let / allow'.

examples.e: give me a glass of water

patterns.label: Greetings & farewells
patterns.structure: nei5 hou2 / zou2 san4 / zoi3 gin3
patterns.note: The openers and closers: 你好 (nei5 hou2, hello), 早晨 (zou2 san4, good morning), 再見 (zoi3 gin3, goodbye). A conversation opens and closes with these.

drills.frameJ: ▢! ngo5 giu3 William.
drills.english: Hello! My name is William.

drills.frameJ: ▢! fan3 dak1 hou2 maa3?
drills.english: Good morning! Did you sleep well?

drills.frameJ: do1 ze6, ▢!
drills.english: Thank you, goodbye!

patterns.label: Sorry & thanks
patterns.structure: deoi3 m4 zyu6 / do1 ze6 / m4 gan2 jiu3
patterns.note: 對唔住 (deoi3 m4 zyu6, sorry), 多謝 (do1 ze6, thank you — for a gift/favour), and the reply 唔緊要 (m4 gan2 jiu3, you're welcome / it's nothing).

drills.frameJ: ▢, ngo5 ci4 dou3.
drills.english: Sorry, I'm late.

drills.frameJ: do1 ze6! — ▢.
drills.english: Thank you! — You're welcome.

patterns.label: Polite words
patterns.note: Everyday courtesies: 唔該 (m4 goi1, excuse me / please / thanks for service), 請 (cing2, please — formal, before a verb), 歡迎 (fun1 jing4, welcome).

drills.frameJ: ▢, ze3 gwo3.
drills.english: Excuse me, let me through.

drills.frameJ: ▢ gwong1 lam4!
drills.english: Welcome (to our shop)!

drills.frameJ: ▢ co5.
drills.english: Please sit down.

patterns.label: Yes & OK
patterns.note: Cantonese has no plain 'yes' — you reply with the relevant word. 係 (hai6, it is / correct) answers a 係 (hai6) question; 得 (dak1, OK / can do) answers a 得唔得 (dak1 m4 dak1) question.

drills.frameJ: keoi5 hai6 m4 hai6 hok6 saang1? — ▢.
drills.english: Is he a student? — Yes.

drills.frameJ: ji4 gaa1 heoi3 dak1 m4 dak1? — ▢.
drills.english: Can we go now? — Sure.

patterns.label: Meeting people
patterns.structure: nei5 giu3 mat1 meng2 / nei5 hou2 maa3 / ngo5 m4 ming4
patterns.note: First-meeting phrases: 你叫乜名 (nei5 giu3 mat1 meng2, what's your name?), 你好嗎 (nei5 hou2 maa3, how are you?), and the very useful 我唔明 (ngo5 m4 ming4, I don't understand).

drills.frameJ: A: ▢ B: ngo5 giu3 William.
drills.english: What is your name? — My name is William.

drills.frameJ: A: nei5 giu3 mat1 meng2? B: ▢ William.
drills.english: What's your name? — My name is William.

drills.frameJ: A: ▢ B: ngo5 hou2 hou2, do1 ze6!
drills.english: How are you? — I'm well, thanks!

drills.frameJ: ▢, cing2 gong2 maan6 di1.
drills.english: I don't understand — please speak slowly.

patterns.label: Making plans
patterns.structure: joek3 / dak1 haan4 / goi2 jat6 / jiu1 cing2
patterns.note: Social planning: 約 (joek3, make plans / arrange), 得閒 (dak1 haan4, free / have time), 邀請 (jiu1 cing2, invite), 改日 (goi2 jat6, another day — a polite rain check).

drills.frameC: 週末得閒,我想▢幾個朋友出嚟。
drills.frameJ: zau1 mut6 dak1 haan4, ngo5 soeng2 ▢ gei2 go3 pang4 jau5 ceot1 lai4.
drills.english: Free at the weekend — I want to make plans with a few friends.
drills.frameE: Free at the weekend — I want to … a few friends out.

drills.frameJ: ting1 jat6 nei5 ▢ maa3? jat1 cai4 heoi3 tai2 hei3.
drills.english: Are you free tomorrow? Let's go see a movie.
drills.frameE: Tomorrow are you …? Let's go see a movie.

drills.frameC: 我生日,想▢你哋嚟我屋企。
drills.frameJ: ngo5 saang1 jat6, soeng2 ▢ nei5 dei6 lai4 ngo5 uk1 kei2.
drills.english: It's my birthday — I want to invite you all to my place.
drills.frameE: It's my birthday — I want to … you all to my place.

drills.frameJ: gam1 jat6 m4 dak1 haan4, bat1 jyu4 ▢ sin1 laa1.
drills.english: Not free today — let's do it another day.
drills.frameE: Not free today — let's do it … instead.

patterns.label: Family relationships
patterns.structure: go4 go1 / dai6 dai2 / ze4 ze1 / mui4 mui2 · je4 je2 / ngoi6 po4
patterns.note: Cantonese splits siblings by age — 哥哥 (go4 go1, older brother), 弟弟 (dai6 dai2, younger brother), 姐姐 (ze4 ze1, older sister), 妹妹 (mui4 mui2, younger sister) — and grandparents by side: 爺爺 (je4 je2) / 嫲嫲 (maa4 maa2) are your father's parents; 外公 (ngoi6 gung1) / 外婆 (ngoi6 po4) your mother's.

drills.frameJ: ngo5 ▢ bei2 ngo5 daai6 loeng5 seoi3.
drills.english: My older brother is two years older than me.
drills.frameE: My … is two years older than me.

drills.frameJ: ngo5 ▢ zyu6 hai2 hoeng1 haa5.
drills.english: My paternal grandfather lives in the village.

patterns.label: Days of the week
patterns.note: Days are 星期 (sing1 kei4, week) + a number: 星期一 (sing1 kei4 jat1, Monday) through 星期六 (sing1 kei4 luk6, Saturday). Sunday breaks the pattern — 星期日 (sing1 kei4 jat6).

drills.frameJ: ngo5 dei6 ▢ heoi3 jam2 caa4.
drills.english: We go for dim sum on Sunday.
drills.frameE: We go for dim sum on …

drills.frameJ: gam1 jat6 ▢, jiu3 faan1 gung1.
drills.english: Today is Monday, have to work.

patterns.label: Colour words
patterns.note: Cantonese colour words end in 色 (sik1, colour): 紅色 (hung4 sik1, red), 藍色 (laam4 sik1, blue), 綠色 (luk6 sik1, green), 黑色 (hak1 sik1, black). Say 呢個係… (ni1 go3 hai6…) to name one.

drills.frameJ: siu1 fong4 ce1 hai6 ▢.
drills.english: The fire truck is red.

drills.frameJ: tin1 hung1 hai6 ▢.
drills.english: The sky is blue.

drills.frameJ: je6 maan5 tin1 hou2 hak1, hai6 ▢.
drills.english: The night sky is dark — it's black.
drills.frameE: The night sky is dark — it's …

drills.frameJ: hoeng1 ziu1 hai6 ▢.
drills.english: A banana is yellow.

patterns.label: Drink orders, your way
patterns.note: Cha chaan teng customisation: 走甜 (zau2 tim4, no sugar), 加冰 (gaa1 bing1, add ice), 少冰 (siu2 bing1, less ice); and 熱飲 (jit6 jam2, hot drink) vs 凍飲 (dung3 jam2, cold drink).

drills.frameJ: dung3 gaa3 fe1 ▢, m4 hou2 taai3 tim4.
drills.english: Iced coffee, no sugar — not too sweet.

drills.frameJ: hou2 dung3 aa3, ngo5 jiu3 ▢.
drills.english: It's cold — I'll have a hot drink.

patterns.label: Cooking actions & ingredients
patterns.structure: zing1 / caau2 / zyu2 / cit3 + jim4 / jau4 / wok6
patterns.note: Cantonese cooking centres on a few methods — 煮 (zyu2, boil), 炒 (caau2, stir-fry), 蒸 (zing1, steam), 切 (cit3, cut) — plus seasonings 鹽 (jim4, salt) and 油 (jau4, oil), all in the 鑊 (wok6, wok).

drills.frameC: 廣東人鍾意▢魚,保持鮮味。
drills.frameJ: gwong2 dung1 jan4 zung1 ji3 ▢ jyu2, bou2 ci4 sin1 mei6.
drills.english: Cantonese people like to steam fish to keep it fresh.
drills.frameE: Cantonese people like to … fish to keep it fresh.

drills.frameJ: go3 tong1 taam5 zo2, gaa1 do1 siu2 siu2 ▢.
drills.english: The soup is bland — add a bit more salt.

drills.english: Before stir-frying, put some oil in the wok first.
drills.frameE: Before stir-frying, put some … in the wok first.

drills.frameJ: zyu2 faan6 zi1 cin4, jiu3 ▢ hou2 di1 so1 coi3.
drills.english: Before cooking, cut the vegetables.

drills.frameC: 炒菜要用個大▢,夠熱先好食。
drills.frameJ: caau2 coi3 jiu3 jung6 go3 daai6 ▢, gau3 jit6 sin1 hou2 sik6.
drills.english: Stir-frying needs a big wok — hot enough to taste good.
drills.frameE: Stir-frying needs a big … — hot enough to taste good.

patterns.label: Emergency calls & actions
patterns.structure: gau3 meng6 / bou3 ging2 / gau3 wu6 ce1
patterns.note: In trouble: 救命 (gau3 meng6, help! / save me!), 報警 (bou3 ging2, call the police), 救護車 (gau3 wu6 ce1, ambulance), 火 (fo2, fire), 走 (zau2, get away). The HK emergency number is 999 (gau2 gau2 gau2).

drills.frameJ: dit3 zo2 lok6 seoi2, daai6 aai3 ▢!
drills.english: Fell in the water — shout for help!

drills.english: The house was burgled — call the police right away.
drills.frameE: The house was burgled — … right away.

drills.english: The kitchen's caught fire — very dangerous!

drills.english: He's injured — call an ambulance quick.

drills.frameJ: jau5 fo2 zuk1, daai6 gaa1 faai3 di1 ▢!
drills.english: There's a fire — everyone get out quick!

patterns.label: Tech actions
patterns.structure: soeng5 mong5 / cung1 din6 / mat6 maa5 / waai6
patterns.note: Everyday tech: 上網 (soeng5 mong5, go online), 充電 (cung1 din6, charge the battery), 密碼 (mat6 maa5, password), and 壞 (waai6, broken) when it stops working.

patterns.label: Workplace actions
patterns.structure: faan1 gung1 / fong3 gung1 / gaa1 baan1 / ceot1 loeng4
patterns.note: The working day: 返工 (faan1 gung1, go to work), 放工 (fong3 gung1, finish work), 加班 (gaa1 baan1, overtime), 出糧 (ceot1 loeng4, payday). 公司 (gung1 si1) is the company.

patterns.structure: gung1 fo3 / soeng5 tong4 / daap3 / hok6 haau6
patterns.note: At school: 功課 (gung1 fo3, homework), 上堂 (soeng5 tong4, go to class), 答 (daap3, answer), 考試 (haau2 si3, exam). The shared root 學 (hok6, learn) ties 學校 (hok6 haau6, school), 學生 (hok6 saang1, student), 同學 (tung4 hok6, classmate).

patterns.note: At the hotel: 入住 (jap6 zyu6, check in), 退房 (teoi3 fong2, check out), 鎖匙 (so2 si4, key), 行李 (hang4 lei5, luggage), 早餐 (zou2 caan1, breakfast). Ask 幾樓 (gei2 lau2, what floor).

patterns.note: Rooms — 廚房 (cyu4 fong2, kitchen), 客廳 (haak3 teng1, living room), 廁所 (ci3 so2, toilet); furniture — 床 (cong4, bed), 枱 (toi2, table), 椅 (ji2, chair); and 門 (mun4, door), 窗 (coeng1, window). 屋企 (uk1 kei2) is home.

patterns.structure: lok6 jyu5 / taai3 joeng4 / fung1 / toi4 fung1
patterns.note: Hong Kong weather: 落雨 (lok6 jyu5, raining), 太陽 (taai3 joeng4, sun), 風 (fung1, wind), 颱風 (toi4 fung1, typhoon), 潮濕 (ciu4 sap1, humid). 颱風 (toi4 fung1) days often mean no work.

patterns.note: Getting active: 運動 (wan6 dung6, exercise / sport), 跑步 (paau2 bou6, run), 游水 (jau4 seoi2, swim), 足球 (zuk1 kau4, football), 打波 (daa2 bo1, play ball). 贏 (jeng4) is to win.

patterns.label: Money handling
patterns.structure: jin6 gam1 / seon3 jung6 kaat1 · zaau2 cin2 / coeng3 cin2 · wu6 hau2
patterns.note: Handling money: 現金 (jin6 gam1, cash), 信用卡 (seon3 jung6 kaat1, credit card), 找錢 (zaau2 cin2, change returned), 唱錢 (coeng3 cin2, change currency), 戶口 (wu6 hau2, account).

patterns.label: Restaurant ordering
patterns.note: At a restaurant: 落單 (lok6 daan1, place an order) at the start, 埋單 (maai4 daan1, ask for the bill) at the end. 餐牌 (caan1 paai4) is the menu, 侍應 (si6 jing3) the waiter.

patterns.label: Taking transport
patterns.note: 搭 (daap3) is the verb for taking public transport — 搭巴士 (daap3 baa1 si2, take the bus), 搭的士 (daap3 dik1 si2, take a taxi). 停 (ting4) means 'stop' (to get off).

drills.frameJ: dou3 laa3, ni1 dou6 ▢.

patterns.label: Buy vs sell
patterns.note: A tricky tone-pair: 買 (maai5, buy — rising tone) and 賣 (maai6, sell — low falling tone). Same character family, opposite meaning, told apart by tone alone.

drills.frameJ: ngo5 soeng2 ▢ ni1 gin6 seot1 saam1.
drills.english: I want to buy this shirt.

patterns.label: Keeping pets
patterns.note: 養 (joeng5) means to keep or raise an animal; 寵物 (cung2 mat6) is a pet. 養狗 (joeng5 gau2, keep a dog).

patterns.note: At an attraction: 排隊 (paai4 deoi2, queue), 入場 (jap6 coeng4, entry), 拍照 (paak3 ziu3, take photos), 門票 (mun4 piu3, ticket), 紀念品 (gei2 nim6 ban2, souvenir).
